name: ADA4610-2ARZ-R7
title: Low-noise precision JFET-input op amps with rail-to-rail output, single, dual and quad
summary: A family of JFET-input op amps for dual supplies of ±5 V to ±15 V: ADA4610-1 (single), ADA4610-2 (dual) and ADA4610-4 (quad). Offset is 0.4 mV maximum in B grade and 1 mV in A grade, bias current 5 pA typical, noise 7.3 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz and 0.45 µV p-p from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz, with 15.4 MHz to 16.3 MHz gain bandwidth, rail-to-rail output and no phase reversal. Uses named for it: instruments, medical equipment, multipole filters, precise current measurement, photodiode amplifiers, sensors and audio. ADA4610-2ARZ-R7 is the A-grade dual in the 8-lead SOIC_N.

circuits.title: Positive peak detector
circuits.description: Both halves of a dual amplifier hold the most positive value VIN has reached. U2A charges C3 through D3 and D4 in series, and R6 returns +PEAK to its inverting input to limit its output; U2B buffers C3 as a unity-gain follower whose output is +PEAK. Between peaks U2A swings low until D2 clamps it, D3 turns off, and R7 pulls the D3-D4 junction up to +PEAK, so D4 sits at zero volts and leaks almost nothing; with U2B's tiny bias current C3 holds its charge a long time. C4 is the 50 pF capacitor between U2A's inverting input and output. C3 should be a low-leakage, low-absorption type such as polystyrene or polypropylene. Turning all the diodes round makes it catch negative peaks instead.

parts.note: U2A is amplifier A (pins 1, 2, 3), U2B amplifier B (pins 5, 6, 7); the circuit applies equally to the ADA4610-1 and ADA4610-4
1N448 should read 1N4148, the type of D3 and D4.

circuits.title: Equivalent preamplifier photodiode circuit
circuits.description: A transimpedance stage for a photodiode run at zero bias (photovoltaic mode). The photodiode, drawn as the diode with its junction resistance RD and total input capacitance CT, feeds the inverting input; the noninverting input is grounded. RF sets the gain as V/ID and CF across it adds a pole that keeps the loop stable against CT. With ID = 100 µA and 10 V out, RF is 100 kΩ; with CF near 7 pF the signal bandwidth is about 250 kHz. RD, typically 1000 MΩ, is far above RF and does not affect the result.

operation.text: ADA4610-1 is one amplifier, ADA4610-2 two and ADA4610-4 four. Packages: ADA4610-1 in 8-lead SOIC and 5-lead SOT-23; ADA4610-2 in 8-lead SOIC, MSOP and LFCSP; ADA4610-4 in 14-lead SOIC and 16-lead LFCSP, all surface mount. The B grade, SOIC only and only for the single and dual, holds offset to 0.4 mV and drift to 4 µV/°C; the A grade allows 1 mV and 8 µV/°C (12 µV/°C in SOT-23).

Built on a 36 V dielectrically isolated process with a P-channel JFET input stage and a rail-to-rail output stage that drives hard and has low dropout whether it sources or sinks. The input stage gives low bias current, wide bandwidth, high gain and low noise, and the output does not reverse phase when the input goes past its common-mode range.
Stable at every gain, including with capacitive loads well over 1 nF, and settling stays fast with large capacitive loads.

A JFET's gate current roughly doubles for every 10 °C rise, and the input bias current follows it. The low supply current keeps the die cool, so the bias current stays low at high ambient without active cooling. Board leakage between traces from poor layout or handling can exceed the amplifier's own bias current.

Internal protection lets either input go 0.3 V beyond the supplies without damage. Beyond that, add a series resistor so the input current stays at 10 mA or less; the bias current, under 1.5 nA up to 125 °C, allows large values.
Specified on dual supplies of ±5 V to ±15 V across −40 °C to +125 °C; the absolute maximum is ±18 V.

Running a section open loop as a comparator raises the supply current: the second stage drives the output mirror hard but cannot close the loop. The output stage limits this excess but does not remove it; with all four ADA4610-4 sections run as comparators the supply draws about 7.5 mA to 8.5 mA, against about 5.8 mA to 6.7 mA as followers. Wire a spare section as a voltage follower with its noninverting input held inside the input voltage range.

Offset was measured on units soldered to FR4 by a JEDEC J-STD-020D reflow and held in an oil bath for 10,000 hours. B-grade parts moved about 5 µV on average over that time, under 2 % of the 400 µV room-temperature limit.

After a preconditioning cycle, offset returns within about 8 µV typical after full cycles from room temperature to 125 °C, to −40 °C and back, which is 1 % of the 800 µV full-range limit. Half cycles, room temperature to 125 °C and back, leave a wider spread.

Photodiode capacitance, typically 30 pF to 40 pF, plus the amplifier's input capacitance (under 10 pF, parasitics included) puts a zero in the loop response that can make it unstable; a capacitor across the feedback resistor fixes it. More bandwidth costs more output noise.
The part can be damaged by electrostatic discharge; handle it with ESD precautions.
